gaps.sentence: The company ___ its first quarterly profit in a decade last spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Last spring' is a finished time reference, so the past simple is required.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: The phone is ringing. Don't worry, I ___ it.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous decision at the moment
gaps.explanation: Decisions made at the moment of speaking use 'will': will answer.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ to traffic every year for repainting in May.
gaps.explanation: A recurring scheduled event takes the present simple.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: This is the second time the printer ___ down this week.
gaps.explanation: 'This is the second time …' is followed by the present perfect.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the same bus to work every morning, even in winter.
gaps.hint: every morning signals a fixed routine
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' describes a fixed routine, which takes the present simple: catches.
